items.q: How much should a dermatology practice spend on Google Ads?
items.a: Depends on service mix and geography — for most single-location practices we start at $3,500–$7,500/month in media spend to hit a statistically meaningful cost-per-booked-visit read within 60 days. Multi-location or cosmetic-heavy practices scale higher. We publish the target CPBV before you commit — no vague 'depends on your goals' answers.

items.q: Are you HIPAA-aware with Google Ads tracking?
items.a: Yes. We configure conversion tracking so no PHI ever hits Google — call tracking runs through BAA-covered platforms, forms scrub sensitive fields before firing pixels, and remarketing lists are built from non-PHI page signals only. We audit any existing pixel or GTM setup before we touch it.

items.q: Do you manage Local Service Ads (LSA) too?
items.a: Yes — LSA is often the first channel we launch for local dermatology. We handle Google verification, badge maintenance, lead review, and dispute filing for non-qualified leads (which you shouldn't be paying for).

items.q: What's a realistic timeline to see results?
items.a: Search and LSA typically show booked-visit signal within 21–30 days. Performance Max needs 4–6 weeks to exit the learning phase. Every month we ship a P&L-formatted report — no black-box dashboards, no cherry-picked screenshots.

items.q: Do you build the landing pages too?
items.a: Yes — Google Ads without a matched landing page is wasted spend. Every campaign gets a service-specific landing page with a booking-first layout, HIPAA-safe form, and CRO iteration built into the retainer.

items.q: What happens if a campaign underperforms?
items.a: Every campaign has a monthly cost-per-booked-visit ceiling agreed upfront. Miss it two months in a row without a clear seasonality reason and the budget rotates into a campaign that's hitting target — no defensive reporting, no sunk-cost pitches.
